title: X-RateLimit-Limit is 300 x registers + 50 and rides every response; a 429 carries the documented title and an RFC 1123 Retry-After, not delta-seconds

source.note: The quota formula is "300 x <number of registers> + 50"; the shipped scenario has two registers, so 650. X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining are documented as present on EVERY response, and the page's Retry-After example is an absolute HTTP-date ("Wed, 15 Jul 2020 15:04:05 GMT"), NOT the delta-seconds every other vendor here uses. The 429 in step 4 is injected by the chaos-demo profile's own rule rather than by spending 650 requests inside one case, so its `message` is the injected fault's and is matched loosely; the documented body sentence ("Rate limiting enforced") belongs to the real limiter and is pinned by tests/unit/lightspeed/test_ratelimit.py. Everything else asserted here -- the status, the `error` title, both headers, and the Retry-After shape -- is the vendor's and is the unit's own. The exact instant is stable because chaos-demo runs on a virtual clock started at 2026-09-04T12:00:00Z and the documented window is five minutes.
